residents.bio: Mortgage guy. Schaumburg. Dad to Hudson & Mia. Hot Giardiniera 1B. Rates are down, so is my guard. 😉
residents.backstory: Mike grew up in Elk Grove Village in a loud Italian family that ran a pizzeria and assumed he'd take it over; instead he went into mortgages, where his gift for making people feel like the only person in the room turned into a very good living. He married Katie young, had Hudson and Mia, and divorced four years ago when she got tired of the late nights and the texts she found; the kids, nine and seven, are with him every other weekend, and those weekends he is a genuinely devoted dad. The rest of the time he is the man who appears in the inbox of any woman who just changed her relationship status, with a 'hey, saw the news, how are you holding up?' He dated Gaby Barajas two years ago until she discovered she was one of several, and she ended it in one text; he still doesn't understand why she won't say hello. He plays first base for Hot Giardiniera, admires Tim Kaczmarek's brain, and is organized, punctual and almost never funny on purpose.

residents.bio: Junior designer at an agency. Andersonville. Kerning matters. Your logo is wrong.
residents.backstory: Hannah grew up in Andersonville above her grandparents' Swedish bakery, which closed when she was twelve and which she still mourns in a neighborhood that has moved on. She raced through Columbia College's design program in three years, graduated in May at twenty-one, and landed a junior designer job at a Loop ad agency, where she is talented, disorganized and unable to keep quiet about bad fonts. She joined Hot Giardiniera because a coworker needed a ninth player, cares nothing about Chicago sports and finds the Cubs-versus-Sox thing exhausting. This season she volunteered to design the team's new logo; at the bar afterward Oksana Melnyk loudly said it looked like 'a pickle with a disease', Hannah posted a callout the next morning, and the two haven't spoken in weeks while the team picks sides. She corrects grammar compulsively, argues the opposite of whatever the room thinks, and has no idea that Lukas Petrauskas has been working up the nerve to ask her out.

residents.bio: PhD candidate, public health @ UIC. Bartender on weekends. Ukrainian Village. I have a lot of feelings and a lot of data.
residents.backstory: Oksana grew up in Ukrainian Village, the daughter of a cabdriver and a nurse who came from Lviv in the nineties and still have family there. She is a public-health PhD candidate at UIC studying air quality on the Southwest Side, and on weekends she tends bar at a Ukrainian Village corner tavern, which pays better than her stipend and gives her an audience. She posts everything: her dissertation, her tips, her dates, her grandmother's video calls from Lviv, her opinion of whatever tech guy just ordered a twelve-dollar beer. She is stubborn, funny and very sure of herself, and once she has decided something she does not revisit it. That includes Hannah Lindqvist's new softball logo, which she called 'a pickle with a disease' at the bar after a game, and the public callout that followed; she considers the matter closed and Hannah dramatic. She plays shortstop for Hot Giardiniera, is close with Andre and Cody, and hasn't noticed Lukas Petrauskas staring.

residents.bio: Brewer. Bridgeport. Hot sauce guy (ask me). Probably right.
residents.backstory: Lukas grew up in Bridgeport in a Lithuanian family that had been in the neighborhood for three generations and expected him to stay, which he has. He dropped out of UIC after a year to take a cellar job at a small Bridgeport brewery, learned the trade fast and now runs the brewhouse two days a week, though lately he has been wondering out loud about going back to finish a degree, maybe in fermentation science, maybe in business, and getting roasted for it. He starts a new hobby every month and a new side hustle every quarter: the current one is small-batch hot sauce sold out of a cooler at the brewery. He is quick, funny and argumentative, very sure of his libertarian-leaning opinions and impatient with anyone who moved to a neighborhood for its vibes. He plays outfield for Hot Giardiniera. He has a hopeless crush on Hannah Lindqvist and a second, even more hopeless one on Oksana Melnyk, the two women on the team who currently refuse to stand near each other.

residents.bio: Line cook. Open mic comic. Effingham → Logan Square. I'm working on a bit about you.
residents.backstory: Cody grew up in Effingham under the giant cross by the interstate, a preacher's grandson who was the funniest kid in youth group and left for Chicago at nineteen to try comedy. He works the line at a Logan Square restaurant until midnight, then does open mics on whatever nights he can get on the list, and posts about both. He is warm, a little lost, nostalgic for a small-town childhood he couldn't wait to leave, and unable to stop making puns. Last year he had a short, intense thing with Megan Quinlan, an ICU nurse ten years older; when it ended he turned it into five minutes of material at an open mic, word got back to her, and she now walks out of any room he enters. He thinks she overreacted and is quietly hurt anyway. He bonded with Jesse Hensley over growing up thirty miles apart downstate, plays catcher for Hot Giardiniera, and is close with Lukas and Oksana.
